column11: Kymriah, CMS Medicare Part B 2024 (drug_demand): $10,678,318.77 over 21 beneficiaries = $508,491.37 per beneficiary a year. HCPCS Q2042 is 'tisagenlecleucel, up to 600 million CAR-positive viable T cells, including leukapheresis and dose preparation procedures, per therapeutic dose', and the same file records 21 dosage units over those 21 beneficiaries, so the per-beneficiary figure is one course per patient and the per-course and per-patient-year prices are the same number. For scale, CMS's October 2026 Part B payment limit file puts Q2042 at $626,315.834 a dose
column12: the 2024 CMS figure is kept rather than the October 2026 payment limit because the book's convention is the per-beneficiary spending series, and because the 2024 figure is what the stopping rate below is measured on. The gap between them, 23%, is three years of ASP drift on a product Medicare bought 21 times in a year; a 21-patient denominator is the real caveat here and it is why this row should move the moment a larger year is available
